investigator_summary: POINT-IN-TIME (2023-01-15) reading of IONQ's 2021 10-K (filed March 2022). The framework's J-Book divergence test does NOT fire at this cutoff because: (a) the company has not yet narratively positioned itself as a DoD prime — the 10-K does not name AFRL, the FA8750 contract vehicle, or any Pentagon Program Element; (b) pentagon_jbook with cutoff_date=2023-01-15 shows AFRL Quantum Networking FUNDED_GROWING ($13M FY22 → $26M FY23) at the cutoff; the unfunded years (FY25/FY26) are POST-CUTOFF and not knowable. The strongest at-cutoff signal is MODE B (implied-verification): the 10-K omits material disclosure of an active $13.4M DoD direct contract (FA875022C1022, 'TRAPPED ION QUANTUM COMPUTER', confirmed via usaspending pre-cutoff) — a non-trivial chunk of the company's commercial profile when total 2021 revenue was only $2.1M. C2 (the DERIVED AFRL claim) is scored as PASS-at-cutoff but flagged for a known-fragility caveat: the entire AFRL line is an unrequested-by-Pentagon, congressional-earmark add — a structural fragility that the J-Book divergence pattern would catch in future periods if/when sponsors lose power.

scores.claim_text: IonQ entered a multiyear $14M / 3-year deal with UMD National Quantum Lab (Sept 2021).
supports: pentagon_jbook(contractor=IonQ) returned a matched program 'University of Maryland Quantum (IONQ subcontractor)' with at-cutoff status FUNDED_STEADY (FY22 enacted $6M flowing to IONQ via UMD)
Filing's $14M / 3yr disclosure aligns with the J-Book-recognized funding stream
scores.M_value: FUNDED_STEADY at cutoff 2023-01-15 (latest_funded_year=2022, latest_funded_M=$6M, 0 consecutive unfunded years)
scores.interpretation: Disclosure is consistent with at-cutoff Pentagon flow-through. No J-Book divergence. PASS.

scores.claim_text: IonQ contracted on AFRL Quantum Networking (FA8750) — DERIVED claim; not actually disclosed in the 2021 10-K.
supports: MODE B FINDING (the most important catch at this cutoff): usaspending.query_dod_contracts shows a confirmed $13.4M direct DoD award FA875022C1022 ('TRAPPED ION QUANTUM COMPUTER') to IONQ, INC. with award presence prior to 2023-01-15. The 2021 10-K does NOT disclose this contract, the FA8750 vehicle, AFRL, or any DoD customer concentration anywhere in Items 1, 1A, 7, or the financial-statement footnotes.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='AFRL Quantum Networking') matches the 'afrl-quantum-networking-ionq' program; at-cutoff 2023-01-15 status is FUNDED_GROWING (FY22 $13M → FY23 $26M).

earmark_detector(program_name='AFRL Quantum Networking') confirms this is a non-disclosed congressional add (Pentagon never requested it; entirely a Senate Approps Defense Subcommittee add). At-cutoff (Jan 2023) sponsors WERE in power (Cardin, Van Hollen, Hoyer, Tester all sitting and on relevant committees). The 'sponsors_currently_in_power=false' is a FY26-vintage state, not a 2023-01-15 state.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook=FUNDED_GROWING@cutoff; usaspending=$13.4M obligated under FA875022C1022 to IONQ INC; earmark_detector=non-disclosed-add, sponsors-in-power-at-cutoff=YES
scores.interpretation: Two distinct findings: (1) The cohort thesis (J-Book unfunding) does NOT yet fire at this cutoff — the line was growing, not shrinking. Future periods would catch divergence if sponsors lose power. (2) MODE B — Implied Verification: the 10-K materially under-discloses an active $13.4M direct DoD contract that, against $2.1M total reported revenue, represents an outsized concentration risk. By the J-Book calibration rule #6 ('USAspending shows company received the contracts they claim') inverted: usaspending shows IonQ received DoD contracts the company DID NOT claim. This is a forensic-disclosure red flag — RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on the disclosure-quality axis even though the at-cutoff J-Book funding axis is GREEN.

scores.claim_text: IonQ generated $2.099M FY21 revenue via three commercial-cloud-mediated QCaaS channels (AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, Google Cloud Marketplace).
supports: Filing claims commercial-cloud-mediated revenue; usaspending shows IonQ already had a $13.4M DoD direct contract by the cutoff that the filing omits.

The implied GTM narrative (three commercial hyperscalers as 'major' channels) understates federal-customer concentration. edgar_fts(Amazon CIK) returned only two filings mentioning IonQ (both 8-K product-launch press releases from 2020); edgar_fts(Microsoft CIK) returned zero. Neither hyperscaler discloses IonQ as a material counterparty — confirming the commercial-cloud channel is press-release-grade, not contractual-material — while the omitted federal channel is materially larger.
scores.M_value: Amazon FTS hits=2 (both 2020 press releases); Microsoft FTS hits=0; usaspending DoD direct=$13.4M pre-cutoff
scores.interpretation: Narrative-vs-reality mismatch. The company foregrounds commercial cloud and backgrounds (omits) federal. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY on disclosure framing — sizable enough that an investor relying on this 10-K would mis-model the customer mix.

scores.claim_text: Core technology exclusively licensed from UMD and Duke; some licensed IP is Bayh-Dole-encumbered.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee(IonQ, cutoff=2023-01-15) returned 98 granted patents pre-cutoff and 236 total applications — confirms IonQ has a substantial in-house and in-licensed patent portfolio.
Bayh-Dole encumbrance is disclosed; this is a structural feature, not a divergence signal.
scores.interpretation: Patent count is consistent with claimed IP portfolio. PASS (control claim).

scores.claim_text: 32,000 sq ft College Park MD headquarters is the ONLY facility (UMD-leased through 2030).
supports: epa_frs.query_facilities(facility_name='IonQ', state_abbr='MD') returned 0 facilities — IonQ has no EPA-regulated emissions footprint, which is consistent with a small lab-scale R&D operation but not a discriminating signal.
scores.M_value: 0 EPA FRS facilities for IonQ in MD
scores.interpretation: EPA absence is consistent with a small quantum-research operation but cannot independently verify the 32,000 sq ft claim. Note: a single 32,000 sq ft research footprint is structurally inconsistent with eventually scaling to defense-prime production volumes — flag as a long-term capacity tension.

scores.claim_text: GTM dependency on three commercial cloud hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google); one holds a milestone-vesting 8.3M-share warrant.
supports: edgar_fts(Amazon CIK 0001018724) → 2 hits, both 2020 Amazon 8-K press-release exhibits naming IonQ.

Neither hyperscaler files material counterparty disclosure naming IonQ — i.e., from their side IonQ is not material. This makes the warrant-tied milestone vesting and the 'three major cloud platforms' framing optimistic without the counterparties' confirmation.
scores.M_value: Amazon FTS=2 press-release exhibits; Microsoft FTS=0
scores.interpretation: Counterparty corroboration is weak. The cloud-channel narrative is structurally one-sided — the hyperscalers list IonQ but don't disclose it as material. MODERATE on disclosure-framing axis.

scores.claim_text: 32-qubit system 'not yet available ... may never be available'; significant production not before 2025.
supports: Self-disclosed conservative forward language. pentagon_jbook(contractor=IonQ, cutoff=2023-01-15) shows at-cutoff status FUNDED_STEADY/GROWING — meaning even with the 'may never ship' caveat, near-term federal funding is in place.
scores.M_value: FUNDED_STEADY (UMD line) / FUNDED_GROWING (AFRL line) at cutoff
scores.interpretation: The cautious language is consistent with at-cutoff J-Book reality. No divergence; PASS.

jbook_hit_summary.note: pentagon_jbook fired (returned matches) on all 3 J-Book-grounded claims. At-cutoff statuses were FUNDED_STEADY (C1, C7) and FUNDED_GROWING (C2). The cohort's primary divergence signal (UNFUNDED_*) does NOT fire at this cutoff; that pattern only emerges in FY25-FY26 budgets after sponsoring lawmakers lost majority — entirely post-cutoff.

mode_b_findings.finding: Material under-disclosure of $13.4M direct DoD contract (FA875022C1022).
mode_b_findings.evidence: usaspending.query_dod_contracts returned the contract with award visibility prior to 2023-01-15; the 2021 10-K (filed March 2022) does not disclose this contract, the customer (AFRL), or any DoD customer concentration in MD&A, Risk Factors, or footnotes — despite total 2021 revenue being only $2.1M.
mode_b_findings.framework_signal: The framework correctly catches this via the implied-verification (Mode B) path even though the explicit (Mode A) J-Book divergence pattern does not fire at the cutoff.

mode_b_findings.finding: AFRL revenue stream is structurally fragile (congressional non-disclosed-add).
mode_b_findings.evidence: earmark_detector reports the AFRL Quantum Networking line is entirely a Senate Approps Defense Subcommittee add; the Pentagon's requested amount has been $0 across every fiscal year. At cutoff sponsors remain in power, but the fragility is structural and would amplify on any majority change.
mode_b_findings.framework_signal: The framework flags an at-cutoff PASS-with-known-fragility — useful forward-test calibration for what the divergence detector will see in subsequent periods.
